question: Can a standard pretrained causal transformer be extended from token sequences to continuous-time, continuous-embedding inputs without retraining, and do duration and embedding interpolations elicit structured intermediate predictions?

key_findings.claim: For piecewise-constant inputs, continuous causal attention reduces exactly to ordinary attention with each key's exponential score multiplied by that token's interval duration.
key_findings.evidence: The integral attention operator is derived as a finite sum weighted by durations d_k; setting every d_k=1 recovers the discrete transformer. Consequently the intervention requires no new learned weights, although it changes the attention normalization whenever durations are nonuniform.

anchors.section: 3 A Continuous Generalisation of Language Models

key_findings.claim: Duration-weighted pretrained models exhibit structured fractional-counting behavior across several model families, but the evidence is based on artificial attention-mass interventions rather than naturally timed language.
key_findings.evidence: Across 200 single-token counting records and six model families, shrinking repeated-word durations yields changing numeric peaks rather than the discrete baseline's constant prediction; the paper reports 190% more unique applicable predictions on average. The valid-record rate is only 59.3% globally because many words do not tokenize to one token.

key_findings.claim: The same duration mechanism changes predictions coherently at larger linguistic units, including arithmetic digit groups and whole event sentences.
key_findings.evidence: When the duration of the two tokens representing 13 is reduced in 24+13, probability shifts from 37 toward 25 as if 13 became 1. When four purchase-event sentences are jointly shortened, Llama3-8B produces peaks corresponding to Alice buying one through four items; the broader event suite reports 205% more unique predictions than the discrete counterfactual.

key_findings.claim: Interpolating between token embeddings produces smooth, sometimes non-monotonic semantic output curves, but smoothness alone is expected from a continuous neural network and does not establish that off-manifold mixtures have linguistic meaning.
key_findings.evidence: Experiments interpolate 40 points between equal-length tokenizations for object pairs and Boolean operators. Across 200 object/property records, 59.3% are valid, the global normalized maximum absolute derivative is 6.214, and 20.79% have a maximum intermediate deviation of at least 0.05 beyond the endpoint range; examples include an intermediate apples/bananas mixture eliciting green more strongly than either endpoint.

key_findings.claim: The construction is empirically approximately translation-invariant in continuous position but not scale-invariant, making token duration a genuine control variable of this operator rather than merely a coordinate change.
key_findings.evidence: Shifting all integration intervals by up to 10 while preserving duration has negligible effect for rotary-position models, whereas scaling every duration changes output distributions. GPT-2 with learned positional embeddings is less exactly invariant but retains the top predicted class under the tested moderate shifts.

method.core_idea: Represent a token sequence as a piecewise-constant function of continuous time, replace causal attention's discrete sum with an integral, and evaluate pretrained transformer weights under arbitrary token durations or interpolated embeddings.
method.mechanism: Analytically integrating attention over constant token intervals yields duration-weighted softmax attention. The implementation supplies a duration vector alongside the usual embeddings and modifies attention weights accordingly; experiments vary selected durations or linearly mix equal-length token embeddings while leaving pretrained parameters fixed.
assumptions: A token's interval length can be treated as a meaningful semantic duration even though pretraining contains no such input channel.
Piecewise-constant embeddings and linear interpolation are useful probes of a model between discrete vocabulary points.
RoPE or related positional computations can be evaluated at the continuous coordinates induced by the intervals.
Changes in next-token probabilities under artificial duration or embedding interventions reveal properties relevant to language representation rather than only local network continuity.

techniques.role: Defines causal self-attention as an integral over a piecewise-constant input history.
Implements the integral exactly as duration-weighted attention using unchanged pretrained parameters.
Shrinks repeated tokens, digit groups, or complete sentences and measures next-token probability peaks.
Samples linear paths between token embeddings to test smoothness and intermediate semantic responses.
Separates changes caused by shifting continuous coordinates from changes caused by rescaling duration.

evaluations.setting: Llama2/3, Phi3, Gemma1/2, and Mistral on 200 single-token word-counting records while a shared duration factor sweeps repeated words.
evaluations.metric: Number and normalized frequency of unique applicable top-prediction peaks; valid tokenization rate.
evaluations.result: The continuous intervention produces 190% more unique predictions than the constant discrete counterfactual on average, with substantial variation by model and only 59.3% globally valid records.
evaluations.baseline: The same pretrained model with all token durations fixed to one.

evaluations.setting: Two-digit addition prompts and four-sentence event-counting stories under group-level duration shrinkage.
evaluations.metric: Probability assigned to original, shortened, intermediate, and unexpected answer labels; unique prediction peaks.
evaluations.result: Predictions shift toward answers consistent with shortened digit groups and with fewer counted events; event experiments report 205% more unique predictions than the discrete counterfactual.
evaluations.baseline: Unmodified discrete-duration prompts and counterfactual constant predictions.

evaluations.setting: Forty-point linear embedding paths for four properties over 50 object pairs, plus Boolean-operator interpolation.
evaluations.metric: Valid equal-tokenization rate, normalized maximum absolute derivative, and maximum interior probability outside the endpoint range.
evaluations.result: Probability curves are generally smooth; global derivative is 6.214, mean endpoint-range excursion is 0.0339, and 20.79% of valid records exceed an excursion of 0.05.
evaluations.baseline: Predictions at the two discrete endpoint embeddings.

limitations: Duration weighting is algebraically an attention-mass reweighting, so the experiments do not by themselves show that natural language or human reasoning is intrinsically continuous in this sense.
Linear embedding paths are usually off the training manifold; smooth probability curves follow from continuous network operations and need stronger semantic controls to support interpretive claims.
The study reports probing behavior rather than accuracy, calibration, robustness, or generation-quality improvements on downstream tasks.
Many setups are excluded by tokenization constraints, and reported aggregate peak ratios depend on hand-specified applicable output classes.
The experiments measure next-token probabilities; argmax text generation remains discrete and may not preserve the apparent continuous trajectory.
The claim that models reason fundamentally differently from humans has no matched human psycholinguistic experiment.
failure_modes: A duration change can merely suppress or amplify attention to a token without corresponding to any interpretable fractional linguistic unit.
Interpolated embeddings can pass through arbitrary high-dimensional regions and produce fluent-looking but non-compositional probability changes.
Tokenizer length mismatches invalidate comparisons and systematically select unusually simple word pairs.
Small probability changes can create many unique argmax peaks while having little practical effect on calibrated generation.
Learned absolute positional embeddings or architecture-specific attention code may break the claimed translation behavior or implementation compatibility.
reusable_insights: A continuous-time generalization of discrete attention can often be implemented exactly through quadrature weights rather than retraining a new architecture.
Translation and scale interventions are useful controls for distinguishing coordinate artifacts from duration-dependent behavior.
Embedding-path probes should report both local smoothness and deviations from endpoint interpolation; the latter is a more discriminating measure of learned nonlinear structure.
Continuous-control claims should be separated into mathematical continuity, semantic coherence, and downstream utility, each with its own evaluation.
open_questions: Can duration controls improve a concrete task such as compression, streaming inference, controllable generation, or multimodal alignment without retraining?
Do structured duration effects survive controls that match attention mass through ordinary logit biases or repeated-token reweighting?
Which paths through representation space stay on a learned semantic manifold better than linear interpolation?
How stable are the results across prompts, seeds, quantization, decoding rules, and larger current models?
Can human experiments with speech rate or temporal grouping test any claimed correspondence between model duration and human processing?

competitive_landscape.title: Vector-Quantized Input-Contextualized Soft Prompts for Natural Language Understanding
competitive_landscape.relationship: Prior continuous-input work in which language models consume learned, non-vocabulary prompt embeddings conditioned on the input.
competitive_landscape.difference: The soft-prompt method learns task-oriented continuous tokens; the target changes attention integration and probes pretrained models with hand-controlled durations and embedding paths without optimization.

competitive_landscape.title: Soft Tokens, Hard Truths: Improving Continuous Chain of Thought via Discrete Tokens and Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current functional competitor using continuous latent token mixtures for language-model reasoning.
competitive_landscape.difference: Soft Tokens, Hard Truths trains continuous reasoning trajectories with reinforcement learning and evaluates task performance; the target is a no-training analytic extension and behavioral probe, not a learned reasoning method.

competitive_landscape.title: Continuous Chain of Thought Enables Parallel Exploration and Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Concurrent continuous-token reasoning approach with theoretical and reinforcement-learning evaluations.
competitive_landscape.difference: That work uses continuous latent thoughts to parallelize search on algorithmic problems; the target studies continuous input time and embeddings in existing causal transformers.

competitive_landscape.title: CIE: Controlling Language Model Text Generations Using Continuous Signals
competitive_landscape.relationship: Directly relevant method for mapping scalar continuous controls into language-model embedding space.
competitive_landscape.difference: CIE fine-tunes interpolated control embeddings for generation attributes and evaluates controllability; the target discovers responses to untrained duration and token-embedding interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Embedding-based In-Context Prompt Training for Enhancing LLMs as Text Encoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Recent evidence that continuous demonstration embeddings can be inserted into an LLM context and optimized for downstream representation quality.
competitive_landscape.difference: The competitor learns continuous in-context embeddings as a practical encoder adaptation; the target uses fixed interpolation paths and duration weights to characterize latent continuity.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after checking continuous-prompt, continuous-control, and continuous-reasoning work: the distinctive contribution is the exact continuous-time attention derivation whose piecewise-constant form allows arbitrary duration probes with unchanged pretrained weights. Continuous embeddings themselves are established, and smooth interpolation is not surprising; the strongest novel evidence is the repeated structured response to duration at token, digit-group, and sentence scales. No practical advantage over ordinary attention reweighting or learned continuous-token methods is yet demonstrated.
